title: Attention Head Universality Across Model Families: Are Induction Heads Really Universal?

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible: validating or refuting universality has broad implications for whether interpretability findings transfer across models. But the direct safety impact is theoretical rather than immediately actionable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: TransformerLens supports 50+ models, and automated induction head detection (prefix match score) exists as a standard protocol. Beginners can run the detection script across models with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused: run an existing detection algorithm across a stratified model sample, report prevalence statistics. The protocol is repetitive and systematic. Clear deliverable (universality report). Achievable in 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: Induction heads are well-established as a universal phenomenon since Olsson et al. (2022), with extensive theoretical analysis in 2025. The original paper already demonstrated emergence across model scales. Recent work extends to selective induction heads and theoretical characterization. However, a systematic empirical survey across diverse model families (not just different scales) with standardized detection metrics has not been published as a standalone study. The incremental value is in the breadth of the empirical survey.

evidence.source: Olsson et al. (2022) - In-context Learning and Induction Heads
evidence.finding: Established that induction heads emerge consistently across model scales and are critical for in-context learning, with a phase change occurring early in training for models of every size with more than one layer.
Studies how transformers implement selective induction heads, extending the basic induction head concept to more complex pattern-matching scenarios.

evidence.source: On the Emergence of Induction Heads (2025)
evidence.finding: Provides theoretical analysis showing training dynamics are constrained to a 19-dimensional subspace with only 3 dimensions accounting for induction head emergence, suggesting architectural universality.
